chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “Water purifies, and it is not purified.”

key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water, the substance used for ritual purification
key_terms.يُطَهَّرُ: it is purified; made pure by something else
key_terms.يُطَهِّرُ: it purifies; it removes ritual impurity or filth in legal context

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith mean when it says that water purifies and is not purified?
ai.summary: This hadith states a foundational ruling regarding water in ritual purity: water serves as a purifier for other things. It also indicates that water itself is not purified by another substance, underscoring its unique legal status in taharah.
